I'm 49 years old, been farming these 60 mu in Quzhou for 25 years. I finished middle school, then came back to the land. I pick up some new variety names from the seed dealer in town and from village meetings, but mostly I do what worked before and watch what the neighbors do. My wife and my son both work off-farm part of the year, so labor is tight during busy times. That means I hire the machinery team for tillage and sowing, and every yuan I spend on urea is a yuan I can't spend on hired help. I have to balance it, but I still won't cut fertilizer below what I know works.

Last year I split the land the same way I'm doing this year: 45 mu for wheat followed by maize, and 15 mu for cotton. The wheat gave me about 530 kg per mu, the maize about 620 kg, and the cotton about 300 kg of seed cotton per mu. I don't want to change a winning formula, so I'm keeping the same layout. Changing crops is risky — if it fails, I lose real money.

For the winter wheat that's already in the ground since last October, I sowed Jinmai 22, an improved variety my neighbor Lao Zhang has used for years. I put 17 kg of seed per mu. Before sowing I spread 50 kg of compound fertilizer 15-15-15 per mu — that gives 7.5 kg nitrogen, 7.5 kg phosphorus, and 7.5 kg potassium. Then at green-up in March I topdress with 20 kg of urea per mu, which is about 9 kg nitrogen. At jointing in April I add another 15 kg urea, about 7 kg nitrogen. So total I'm putting down about 21 kg nitrogen, 7.5 kg phosphorus, and 7.5 kg potassium per mu. Some people might say that's a lot of nitrogen, but three years ago I cut back to 15 kg and lost nearly 100 kg per mu in yield. I won't make that mistake again. A bag of urea is 100 yuan, but losing a harvest costs thousands.

I irrigate the wheat four times: the winter water before the freeze, the green-up water in March, jointing water in April, and grain-filling water in May. Each irrigation costs me electricity from the well pump, about 25-30 yuan per mu, but without it the yields crash. I spray pesticide twice: once in April for aphids, and once in May for rust and powdery mildew. The dealer gives me the same two-bottle mix every year.

For tillage on the wheat land, I hire the rotary tiller in October after the maize comes off. They charge 40 yuan per mu.

For summer maize, I plant Zhengdan 958 — it's a hybrid, everyone here uses it because it tolerates the heat. I sow 2.5 kg per mu right after wheat harvest in early June. There's no time to plough; the season is only about 100 days. I do no-tillage direct seeding with the machine, otherwise I miss the good moisture window. I put 40 kg of compound 15-15-15 down at sowing, which is 6 kg each of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. Then at the 6-leaf stage I side-dress 25 kg of urea, about 11.5 kg nitrogen. Total nitrogen is about 18 kg per mu, phosphorus 6 kg, potassium 6 kg. I plan two irrigations: one when I side-dress, and one at tasseling in late July. If the rain is good I might skip one, but I budget for two.

Maize gets two pesticide sprays: one when the seedlings are small for armyworm, and one at the big喇叭口 stage for corn borer. That's what the dealer recommends and what I've always done.

The 15 mu of cotton I keep because last year's price was decent, around 7.5 yuan per kg for seed cotton. I plant Xinluzao 26, an improved variety, 1.8 kg of seed per mu. Cotton needs deep ploughing in April so the roots can go down, so I pay for ploughing at 50 yuan per mu. Base fertilizer is 50 kg of compound 15-15-15 and 15 kg of potassium sulfate per mu. That gives about 7.5 kg nitrogen, 7.5 kg phosphorus, and about 10 kg potassium. Then I topdress twice with 15 kg urea each time, about 7 kg nitrogen each time. Total nitrogen is about 21 kg per mu. Cotton needs the extra potassium or the bolls drop off.

I irrigate cotton three times: at flowering, at boll setting, and at boll opening. Pesticide four times: for aphids, red spider mites, bollworm, and one preventive spray in August when the humidity gets high. Cotton is a lot of work, which is why I only keep 15 mu.

My expected yields this year: wheat 550 kg per mu, maize 650 kg per mu, and cotton 320 kg per mu. I'm not trying anything new. I do what I did last year, I watch my costs, and I put in enough fertilizer to make sure I don't lose yield. That's how I've kept this farm going for 25 years.
